questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Quality of education and personal connection to the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite hard

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a campus tour and a welcome lecture.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student dorm

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Cantine on campus and kitchen in the dorm

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The dorms reserved for exchange students are not very socially active, so I would recommend to participate in the events that involve the whole dorm.
The hygiene is also horrendous, so if you are sensitive to that, consider living somewhere else.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Information about courses, classes, schedules, exams and formal requirements are very hard to find, especially before you arrive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied through a website I recieved a link to. After I arrived I had to show up to recieve a piece of paper with important codes for course and exam registration and to recieve my student ID.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange staff were helpful when I emailed them my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. I had to plan my courses using the course catalogue from the year before. Also the course catalogues are hard to find and navigate. Furthermore, they are seldom very accurate.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to email the staff your questions. It can take very long to find information without their help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were master courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Quantum Field Theory, Theoretical Solid State Physics, Applied Photonics, Fundamentals in the Physics of Macromolecules and molecular systems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Quantum Field Theory was taught by Professor Klose, who is very competent and charismatic. It is quite challenging though.

questions.answer: I went home more often than I had thought

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Humboldt University has a sports program for students and staff that is very cheap

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Mostly talks about diversity. There was also a weekly movie evening on campus in one of the auditoriums.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make use of the sports program.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city, go to weird bars and cafes, go to clubs. The Staatsoper has cheap tickets if you arrive 30 minutes before a show that is not sold out (which they seldom are). Take a day trip to Potsdam.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The local culture is similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you can I would try to learn German. Otherwise make use of the sports program and the activities at the dorm. The Erasmus network also host events for exchange students specifically.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier was sometimes challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The weirdness and creativeness of Berlin. A lot of areas of Berlin seem like they belong to the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't hesitate to ask staff when you have questions
Please note that the science campus is located in Adlershof, which is about one hour from the city center
The exam period is split up into two and most students take half of their exams in the first and the other half in the second. I recommend doing the same if possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you need to find housing with other people, search for Wohngemeinschaft.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exhange experience was learning to be more independent both socially and academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was finding a social circle in a new city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
